detail.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

[KDA team](https://github.com/NVlabs/kda) optimizes GDP decode and inference on GB300 by reducing redundant kernel work, tensor copies, CUDA graph replay validation overhead, and greedy sampling overhead.

Changes
- Load GDP query and decay inputs only in the Householder steps that use them (`decode_prepare`).
- Prefetch the next step's recurrent inputs for multi-token (speculative) decode, and store only the final Householder output of each token in a compact `[request, token, head, dim]` layout (`compact_output`), removing the slice + contiguous copy after the kernel.
- Keep the speculative-decode output batch-first so the dynamic path flattens it without a copy.
- Avoid copying transposed weights in the Triton batch-invariant TE GEMM path (DeepGEMM and non-transposed layouts are unchanged).
- Tests: compact output, padding rows with non-finite inputs, full-mixer speculative forward vs. decode oracle, strided-weight bit-exactness, and determinism replays for compact output and M ∈ {1, 2, 3}.

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: None; this PR optimizes existing inference paths.

## Performance

1× GB300, `mcore_ci_dev` image (torch 2.14.0a0 nv26.8, Triton 3.8.0, TE 2.19). Shapes of the GDP 800M hybrid recipe (hidden 1024, 32 GDP heads, head dim 64, 8 groups, state 128, M = 3), fp32 recurrent caches, random weights, B = 32, CUDA-graph replay. Paired ABBA, 6 processes per arm, main `e8a302ac5` vs. this PR. Generated tokens are bitwise identical between the two.

| Case | main p50 (µs) | PR p50 (µs) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| GDP decode (`ssm_decode`), S=1 | 32.5 | 27.7 | 1.17× |
| GDP decode (`ssm_decode`), S=4 | 103.8 | 86.6 | 1.20× |
| GDP mixer forward, default, S=1 | 47.1 | 42.1 | 1.12× |
| GDP mixer forward, default, S=4 | 120.9 | 101.1 | 1.20× |
| GDP mixer forward, batch-invariant Triton, S=1 | 182.2 | 92.6 | 1.97× |
| GDP mixer forward, batch-invariant Triton, S=4 | 228.1 | 134.1 | 1.70× |
| Full-model decode step, default, S=1 | 3769 | 3692 | ≈1.0× (host-bound) |
| Full-model decode step, batch-invariant Triton, S=1 ¹ | 9168 | 5558 | 1.65× |

¹ Batch-invariant attention needs FA3/FA4, which the CI image lacks, so this row was measured in an FA4 environment (torch 2.12.1, Triton 3.7.1, TE 2.20.2). A full-model S=4 step needs MTP heads and is measured at the mixer level only.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [x] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [ ] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [ ] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

### Code review

Feel free to message or comment @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall to help accelerate your merge into main. The less complex your PR is, the faster it will be approved and merged!

All PRs start as **draft**. If you open a non-draft PR, it will be automatically converted to draft.

#### Step 1: Mark PR as "Ready for Review"

1. When your PR is ready, click **Ready for Review**.
2. An oncall reviewer is auto-assigned and expert reviewers are notified based on your changes.
   - Some PRs may jump straight to step 2. This is determined by `.github/CODEOWNERS`.

:warning: Only mark as ready once merge-conflicts are resolved and the CI is passing.
Final Review might get declined if these requirements are not fulfilled.

#### Step 2: Final Review

For PRs that change `megatron/core`, once all expert reviewers have approved, the `Final Review` label is applied **automatically** and final reviewers are assigned.

For PRs outside `megatron/core`, this step is skipped.

#### Step 3: Approved

Once all required reviewers have approved, the `Approved` label is applied **automatically**.

### Merge

Any member of [mcore-engineers](https://github.com/orgs/NVIDIA/teams/mcore-engineers) will be able to merge your PR.

inline_comments.body: Do we need the changes in this file? This seems more invasive than the other GDP-specific changes

These checks were removed because token-only padding is determined independently of the SSM batch-invariant flag.

The existing CUDA graph bucket builder checks the global batch-invariant kernel switch and rounds token_count up to a multiple of 64, while leaving the request counts unchanged. For example, at TP=1 with no speculative tokens, a decode bucket can contain 64 token rows but only 40 decode request slots. The remaining 24 rows have no corresponding request or SSM state slot.

This can also occur when context.batch_invariant_mode is false. GDP already rejects config.batch_invariant_mode=True in the existing mixer code (https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/megatron/core/ssm/gated_delta_product.py#L560-L566). The comment above the assertion explicitly allows GDP to use batch-invariant attention/GEMM kernels without enabling batch-invariant SSM execution. Therefore, the context flag cannot determine whether token-only graph padding is present; trimming and restoring those rows must be handled independently.

Therefore, the first change always slices the decode partition to decode_req_count * (1 + num_speculative_tokens) before entering the recurrent kernels. The second restores any missing rows with zeros before the output projection, using the actual input projection row count.

For Mamba with batch_invariant_mode=True, this preserves the previous trim-and-pad behavior. Without extra padding, no rows are removed and no zero-padding allocation is needed. I verified both revisions on 4×GB300: all 43 selected Mamba regression tests passed, and the targeted Mamba batch-invariant comparisons preserved outputs and state buffers bit for bit.

inline_comments.body:
The padding contract is unchanged; the zeroing has been moved into the recurrent kernel’s existing output stores, in both the regular and prefetched loops:

```
tl.store(
    p_o,
    tl.where(i_s >= 0, b_o, 0).to(p_o.dtype.element_ty),
    mask=mask_v,
)
```

A negative state index now explicitly stores zero at that request’s output address, even if its recurrence produces NaN/Inf. The store is still performed for padding rows, so it overwrites any stale output-buffer contents. Persistent-state reads/writes and intermediate snapshot writes remain guarded by i_s >= 0.

The outer masked_fill_ is therefore redundant. Removing it avoids the separate mask construction and masking kernel launch, while preserving the output semantics for valid requests.

Regression tests poison padding inputs with NaNs and verify zero outputs and unchanged unused state/snapshot slots, covering single-token and speculative decode, as well as compact output.

This change is confined to the GDP recurrent kernel. Mamba uses separate SSM kernels and does not call this function.

Thanks for the suggestion. I have added an assertion in the positive-padding branch, equivalent to:

```
assert (
   padding_token_count == 0
   or context.batch_invariant_mode
   or is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled()

```

By “global kernel mode,” I meant the existing process-wide switch controlled by enable_batch_invariant_mode() / set_batch_invariant_mode() (https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/megatron/core/transformer/custom_layers/batch_invariant_kernels.py#L1818). The CUDA graph bucket builder reads this switch for 64-token alignment. Enabling it does not update the model configuration or context.batch_invariant_mode.

The existing GDP CUDA graph test (https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/test_gdp_cuda_graph_e2e.py#L166-L175) uses these switches independently. I reproduced the configuration with the global switch enabled and the context flag disabled: 40 decode requests produce a 64-token bucket, requiring 24 padding rows. The assertion allows this valid case.

With both switches disabled, the tested production buckets and real-engine cases had zero token-only padding. I also added negative tests that reject unexpected padding with both switches disabled.
